objective: Publish a versioned contract that separates proposed requirements from verified implementation facts and deterministically routes changes through spec-first or code-first handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid document state, when it is validated, then kind, state transitions, ownership, repository/revision provenance, source anchors, verifier, timestamp, tool version, sensitivity, and freshness conform to the published JSON schema.

Given invalid transitions, stale observed SHAs, or speculative text without an explicit marker, when fixtures are validated, then they are rejected and proposed content is never promoted automatically.
Given at least 12 representative change scenarios, when routing is evaluated, then each has an expected spec-first or code-first classification and a documented human override path.

Given concurrent branches, missing or stale evidence, generated/vendor/secret/licensed content, and opt-in/out configuration, when the policy is applied, then conflict, exclusion, and fail-open behavior are explicit; approved contract and security gates remain enforceable.
Given the published source-of-truth table, when GitHub issue, actual code, approved spec, Hindsight, and generated wiki disagree, then ownership and precedence are unambiguous.
Given schema fixtures and migration examples, when maintainers validate the contract, then current-version and migration behavior are reproducible without a redundant event ledger or global run lock.
nonGoals: Implement the spec workflow, reconciliation engine, or UI; those are downstream issues.
Build or select an external index service; treat Git-versioned contract documents and schema as the initial source, with an adapter path documented.
Reimplement dependency, reproducibility, acceptance, or memory systems covered by #126, #130, #132, #134, and #146.
risks: The contract affects cross-project routing and provenance semantics. Mitigate with a versioned schema, explicit migration examples, fixture coverage for stale SHAs and invalid transitions, opt-in defaults, and no automatic promotion of proposals. The initial Git storage assumption is reversible.
dependencies: Epic #174; parallel foundation #175 is closed. Align contract interfaces with #126, #130, #132, #134, and #146; no blocking dependency remains for defining the document and schema.
suggestedWorkBreakdown: Inspect adjacent issue contracts; write the concise normative contract and source-of-truth table; publish schema plus valid/invalid transition and stale-SHA fixtures; add at least 12 classification scenarios and override rules; document privacy exclusions, per-project modes, conflict/freshness policy, and migration/retention; review against downstream issue interfaces.
